thread.title: UPDATE: Apple $1 trillion? Here's the plunge that followed the first company to get there

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Apple $1 trillion? Here's the plunge that followed the first company to get there
text:
By Shawn Langlois, MarketWatch
Be careful what you wish for.
Apple (AAPL) , much to the joy of shareholders and fanboys everywhere, could soon become the first U.S. company to reach a valuation of $1 trillion. A nice earnings beat (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-show-why-you-can-expect-more-1000-iphones-2018-07-31) and a 5% push for the stock on Wednesday could give Apple the back-stretch boost it needs to beat Amazon (AMZN) to that lofty level.
Globally, however, the 13-figure mark was apparently breached more than a decade ago, when PetroChina (0857.HK) enjoyed a face-melting debut in Shanghai. But the celebration didn't last long, as you can see by this chart.
Bloomberg calculated that the collapse (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2017-10-29/the-biggest-stock-collapse-in-world-history-has-no-end-in-sight), which it says is "the biggest stock slump in world history," cost shareholders about $800 billion, thanks to government attempts to limit the kind of speculation that led to that initial surge.
Of course, similarities with Apple pretty much begin and end with that $1 trillion valuation, although PetroChina's implosion in Shanghai is a reminder of the brutal and finicky nature of the stock market.
At last check, Apple was dancing around in record territory with a 5% gain to $200 a share, just a few bucks short of that $1-trillion mark.
See also: Apple path to $1 trillion accelerates as consumers flock to pricey iPhones (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-path-to-1-trillion-accelerates-as-consumers-flock-to-pricey-iphones-2018-08-01)
-Shawn Langlois; 1251ET
